failures.criterion: No periodic poll: a standby takes the publisher hold only when the hold is released, when the timer to its lapse fires, or when its own NATS connection changes (plan decision 8 and the plan's Run loop; lease.go's Run comment says the same)
failures.evidence: Red test TestAStandbyDoesNotTryTheHoldForEveryEventTheHolderWrites (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox/lease_test.go, commit 6ebf4be0). `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<pg> go test -count=1 -run TestAStandbyDoesNotTryTheHoldForEveryEventTheHolderWrites ./internal/dispatch/outbox/` fails at 63e05008 with 'the standby sent 98 takes of the publisher hold and 98 reads of its lapse while the holder wrote 100 events, want at most 3 of each'. Cause: the outbox has one wake channel. listen() signals it on every dispatch_events NOTIFY and wakeOnCommits on every commit, and standby() selects on that same channel, so each event makes each standby send takeHold (insert into duty_holds ... on conflict, which locks the holder's row) and holdExpiry. Measured on real processes with pg_stat_statements (two envoy-dispatch processes, 40 comments/s for 10 s): 601 takes and 601 lapse reads from the standby, against 1 of each in 10 s idle. A throwaway fix in a scratch copy (a second wake channel for the standby, fed only by the release NOTIFY, OnConnected and the NATS change) makes the test pass with 0 and 0, and the five lease rows still pass.

observations: CI at 63e05008: Tests/test red on packages/daemon TestTheSameDeployRunDeliveredTwiceWakesOneLook ('timed out waiting for the look's start row resuming the implementer'). This PR does not change packages/daemon, and the base 2df3353c passed Tests. This pod cannot run that test because it needs Docker. lint, typecheck and build passed; envoy-go, envoy-go-race and dispatch-multiprocess were still queued when read.

A holder with a serving port (role.go:154-163): the outbox counts the stream's acknowledgement of the stored copy as the receipt. The listener routes that copy by its envelope topic, a role topic, to roleTopicDelivery, which ACKs a roleForwardDedupePrefix frame without delivering it (cmd/listener/delivery.go:427). So such a holder does not get the event until dispatch://INFRA-594 (todo) lands. On main the listener's core forward to such a holder (delivery.go:491) seems to end in receipt_timeout as well, so this does not look like a new loss; spec departure 2 was accepted on that basis. This is an inference from the code; I did not run it.
The batch log 'dispatch outbox: published batch events=1' is also written for a batch whose sends were released for NATS loss (17:01:00.134 in the manual run). It counts sends, not publishes.
